newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil stevedores say in talks over Santos dispute.
newsitem.headline: Brazil stevedores say in talks over Santos dispute.

text.p: Brazilian stevedores said they were due to meet officials from steel firm Companhia Siderurgica Paulista (Cosipa) to discuss a dispute which has paralyzed Cosipa's operations at Santos port.

The two sides were scheduled to meet at 1100 local/1400 GMT, said Abelardo Fernandes, president of the National Stevedores' Union. But it was unclear whether the meeting would take place in Sao Paulo or Santos, he added.
A spokeswoman for Cosipa said she could not confirm if any negotiations were to take place.

Twenty-six stevedores have been occupying two vessels at Cosipa's private terminal at the port for more than a week in protest against the firm's decision to use its own workers to conduct loading and unloading at the terminal.

The action has effectively stopped all of Cosipa's operations at the port. Military police officers are stationed on the pier but have so far failed to carry out a judge's order to evacuate the workers.
The stevedores said they would immediately call a strike if the police tried to evict them or if Cosipa allowed any new vessels to dock at the terminal and tried use its own workers.
